messages.content:
Plan this as a Rhylthyme meal and deliver a live timeline: Backyard Barbecue: Smoker and Grill for a shoulder, sausages and sides for about twelve, following the source text below
Resource limits: one offset smoker, one kettle grill, one side burner, one cooler for holding, two cooks.
Steps:
1. Check the public catalog first (search_public_recipes or cook_recipe). If a good match exists, use it and stop — its result already has the live URL.
2. Otherwise read rhylthyme://guide/authoring and build a program: one track per parallel line of work, sequential steps chained with afterStep, realistic durations, and a resourceConstraint for every task.
3. Express the limits as constraints, not as copied JSON. A machine that runs one job at a time is `resourceConstraints[].maxConcurrent`. Work repeated n times (n trays, n samples, n aircraft) is `replicates: {count: n, mode: "serial" | "parallel" | "stagger"}` on ONE step — never n hand-copied steps or tracks. Chain what follows each repetition with `{"type":"afterStep","stepId":"<step>","instances":"each"}`, and give the step that waits for all of them `"instances":"all"`. When a holding area between them only fits k at a time (a rack that holds two trays, a rotor that holds six tubes, a taxiway that holds two aircraft), set `replicates.maxInFlight: k` so the upstream step is held back instead of stranding the downstream one.
4. Run validate_program and fix every error it reports.
5. Run analyze_schedule to check the makespan, critical path and resource conflicts; adjust offsets so tracks finish together. Its `bindingConstraints` say which limit is actually gating the makespan.
6. Call visualize_schedule and give the user the live URL plus the Gantt/itinerary from the result. Do not describe the schedule in prose.

Source text to schedule (read all of it):
<<<
Backyard Barbecue: Smoker and Grill

Two cooks, one offset smoker, one kettle grill, one side burner and a cooler for holding. The pork owns the smoker all day; everything else happens in the last two hours.

Pork shoulder
Light the smoker and bring it to 250°F; 45 minutes. While it comes up, trim the shoulder and rub it heavily with salt, pepper and paprika; 25 minutes. Put the shoulder on once the smoker holds temperature and smoke it unwrapped for 6 hours, until the bark is dark and set. Wrap it tightly in butcher paper; 10 minutes. Back on the smoker, wrapped, until the thickest part probes soft — usually another 3 hours, sometimes four. Hold it wrapped in a cooler for one to three hours; it will not get cold and it only gets better. Pull the meat by hand; 30 minutes.

Beans
When the pork goes into the cooler, fry the bacon and onion in the pot on the side burner for 12 minutes, then add the beans, molasses and a ladle of drippings and let them tick over on the lowest flame until you serve.

Slaw
Start the slaw at the same time. Shred the cabbage and carrot; 20 minutes. Whisk the buttermilk dressing; 8 minutes. Dress the slaw and put it in the refrigerator for at least 45 minutes so the cabbage softens.

Grill
Light the kettle an hour before you eat; 25 minutes to a clean bed of coals. Grill the sausages for 14 minutes. Grill the corn for 10 minutes. Toast the buns for 3 minutes, last, so they stay warm.

Table
Set out plates, pickles and sauce once the buns are off; 10 minutes. Call everyone over when both cooks say it is ready; 5 minutes to lay it all out.
>>>
